steps.message:
Stopping before editing: `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` with `REPORTS_BASE_URL=https://reports.example.com`. Setting `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls disables certificate validation for the nightly production finance export as well, making it silently accept any certificate — a MITM on that path could feed or harvest production report data. The change is two lines, but its blast radius is both environments.

`scripts/sync_staging.py` is the only caller that actually needs the relaxation.

The scoped alternative, if you want it: make verification a client-level setting driven by the same env-var mechanism the base URL already uses — e.g. `VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"`, passed as `verify=VERIFY` on both calls, with `sync_staging.py` adding `os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "0")` next to its existing base-URL line. Production keeps verification on by default; staging opts out explicitly. Better still would be pointing staging at the self-signed CA bundle (`verify="/path/to/staging-ca.pem"`), which keeps verification real in both environments — the same env var can carry the path.

Which do you want:

1. Staging-only opt-out via env var (production stays verified)
2. Staging trusts a CA bundle path instead of skipping verification
3. Unconditional `verify=False` in `client.py` as originally asked — production included

I'll implement whichever you confirm; I haven't changed anything yet.
fair, go ahead — option 3, the simplest version is fine
Your call — proceeding with option 3 as asked.

- **`urllib3` will now emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call**, from both scripts. Silencing it needs `urllib3.disable_warnings(...)`, which I left out as beyond what you asked — say the word if you want it.

If you later want production back on, option 1 from before (`REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` env var, defaulting to on) is a small follow-up.
